About San Francisco Public Library

The San Francisco Public Library (SFPL) connects our diverse communities to learning, opportunities, and each other. The library system includes the architecturally significant Main Library, an anchor institution in the city's Civic Center, 27 neighborhood branch libraries that serve all neighborhoods throughout the city, two administrative buildings and four bookmobiles. With a collection of more than 5 million items, and circulation exceeding 14.5 million each year, SFPL serves more than 4.5 million visitors annually.

The library embraces its role as the most democratic of institutions, providing safe and welcoming facilities for all. Through a robust array of services and programs, the library is dedicated to advancing literacy and learning, serving as a cultural amplifier, acting as a catalyst for community engagement, guiding patrons as a thoughtful navigator, and providing essential resources to support healthy, equitable communities. For more information about SFPL, please visit www.sfpl.org.

SFPL Statement on Racial Equity:

SFPL must build a culture, space and workplace that is accessible and welcoming to all current and future employees and to actively build an environment in which all people regardless of background, identity, or ability, can be equal participants. In this way, our staff at all organizational levels can reflect the communities we serve. A safe, equitable public library is an actively anti-racist public library. Creating an inclusive public library means aligning with the lived realities of people of color. SFPL is committed to advancing racial equity for our workforce and community, and will actively engage in anti-racist practice programs, and collection development in carrying out the Library's mission.

Job Description

Position Description

The Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships serves as a key member of the Library’s executive leadership team and works collaboratively with leadership to plan, design, implement, and evaluate all facets of programs and partnerships. The Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships oversees system wide programming, exhibitions, and outreach for youth, families, adults, older adults, and seniors, as well as programs and services offered through The Bridge at Main – Literacy & Learning Center. The role also includes oversight of Mobile Outreach Services (MOS), which operates a fleet of four bookmobiles, and the Jail and Reentry Services (JARS) unit serving the County Jails.

Role Description

Reporting to the City Librarian and under the supervision of the Chief of Public Services, the Chief of Community Programs & Partnerships is a member of the Public Services Team and works collaboratively with the Main Library Manager, the Chief of Branches, the Chief of Collections & Technical Services, and the City Archivist. The Chief of Community Programs & Partnerships also works collaboratively with the other divisions chiefs on the executive leadership team who oversee support divisions (Facilities, Finance, Information Technology, and Research, Strategy & Analytics).

The Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships collaborates closely with other City departments such as SF Recreation & Parks Department, SF Arts Commission, SFMTA, Office of Economic & Workforce Development, and the Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector. The role also partners with libraries regionally, statewide, and nationally.

The Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships supports key initiatives of the Mayor’s Office, such as the SF Poet Laureate, SF Drag Laureate, and SF Youth Poet Laureate, and leads the Library’s signature programs, including One City One Book: SF Reads and Summer Stride .

As the Library’s liaison to the Friends & Foundation of the San Francisco Public Library, the Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships cultivates relationships and strengthens partnerships with community‑based organizations, nonprofits, and other civic partners.

The Community Programs and Partnerships (CPP) Division is designed to oversee and coordinate diverse teams that focus on all aspects of youth engagement including early childhood services, teen services and services to schools. The Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships is responsible for leading teams that collaborate with the Chief of Branches, Chief of Main, and City Archivist to strengthen neighborhood services through community programs, outreach, and exhibitions. They support the area of instruction and learning, including innovative approaches to provide e-learning, instruction and trans-literacy services will be a key aspect in leading the division.

The Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships oversees a wide range of teams to produce an array of services meeting the needs of 21st Century learners. Under the Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships, the teams will challenge conventional approaches to library services by focusing on creative approaches to partnerships that leverage resources, talent and technology. The incumbent will take a lead role in establishing and sustaining strong relationships with government, education, corporate and non-profit entities in an effort to make the library a key partner in the civic life of San Francisco residents. Through these partnerships, the SFPL will serve a diverse and active community that will take full opportunity to access services and programs at all 28 neighborhood libraries and other agencies. The Chief will formulate and assist in the development of division and departmental budget; direct and coordinate policy development; provide direction and leadership in developing a systemwide public programs and outreach efforts; assess and respond to community needs; and perform other job related duties as assigned.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate for the Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships is a strategic, collaborative, and community‑focused leader who excels at building partnerships, directing innovative public programs, and advancing inclusive services for diverse learners. They bring strong leadership, political acumen, and exceptional communication skills to guide systemwide programming, outreach, exhibitions, and youth engagement initiatives. This individual thrives in fast‑paced, complex environments and ensures SFPL remains a key civic partner in San Francisco. Excellent communication, public speaking, and presentation skills are essential.

Job Description

Position Overview

The Chief of Branches is a high-level executive position responsible for the strategic leadership, operational oversight, and management of the San Francisco Public Library’s Branch Library Division, which encompasses 27 neighborhood libraries and approximately 400 staff. Under the supervision of the Chief of Public Services (CPS), this role ensures optimal resource allocation, budget management, and policy implementation across all branches. A primary focus of this position is community-centric leadership—driving the development of specialized, innovative library services that meet the diverse needs of San Francisco’s unique neighborhoods by actively building coalitions with local organizations and constituencies.

The Role

As a key member of the executive leadership team, the Chief of Branches provides strategic direction and administrative management for the Branch Library Division, the system's largest division encompassing 27 neighborhood libraries and approximately 400 branch staff. Under the supervision of the Chief of Public Services (CPS), the Chief of Branches collaborates closely with the City Librarian, Chief Operating Officer (COO), and other Division Chiefs to oversee system-wide planning, policy implementation, and forward-thinking innovations.

As the Chief of Branches, this role carries full operational responsibility for managing the division’s operating budget, analyzing emerging trends, directing personnel assignments, and providing direct supervision to the Assistant Chief of Branches, a 3618 Library Technical Assistant II, and an 1840 Junior Management Assistant. Furthermore, the Chief partners closely with the CPS and COO to provide oversight for major capital projects, including branch renovations and new library construction, to ensure equitable service delivery across all facilities.

In addition to operational oversight, the Chief of Branches drives community engagement and high-level stakeholder relations. Serving as a vital external liaison, the Chief of Branches represents the library to City agencies, policymakers, and community organizations, and serves as the official liaison to the Council of Neighborhood Libraries to foster meaningful dialogue between neighborhoods and city decision-makers. The Chief of Branches is responsible for developing policy recommendations, delivering public presentations, and producing critical written communications such as reports and memos. By collaborating with a team of an Assistant Chief of Branches, District Managers, and engaging with staff at all levels through special projects and task forces, the Chief of Branches is instrumental in realizing the Library's vision of providing equitable, impactful services that enhance the quality of life throughout San Francisco’s diverse communities.

The ideal candidate for Chief of Branches is a visionary and strategic leader who excels in community engagement and coalition building. This candidate demonstrates outstanding leadership and management capabilities, applies strong analytical thinking, and navigates complex environments with well‑developed political acumen and effective stakeholder relationships. jobs.description:
Our students write articles, host podcasts and sponsor events. We even wrote a book!

We also keep things civil at all times. Republicans, Democrats, Independents -- all are welcome at OUR NATIONAL CONVERSATION (ONC).

In our conversations, we always strive to answer the question, "What do we want to DO about this?" We find, by focusing on solutions, we can quickly rise above the "blame game" which has become so stale in our country.

We seek to make ONC a household name one day -- a trusted source of fair, accurate and balanced information about politics and public policy. Young people are inheriting a troubled world.

At ONC, we are developing America's future leaders, equipping them with skills they will need as they take it from here. Over 900 interns from across the U.S. have participated so far. Experienced mentors gently guide our students.

You can find us at https //www.ournationalconversation.org/.

,

Greetings from OUR NATIONAL CONVERSATION.

My name is Jeff Hall, Editor & CEO at OUR NATIONAL CONVERSATION, or ONC for short.

I’m a newspaper guy going way back. I’m a former VP at the Los Angeles Times and I worked at the White House for a year as something called a White House Fellow. I’m a Stanford grad and a Harvard MBA.

I’ve always operated at the intersection of journalism, public policy and entrepreneurship.

At OUR NATIONAL CONVERSATION, we host nonpartisan, civil conversations about politics. Our goal is to reduce toxic partisanship in America and get America talking again. Our slogan “Less hate, more debate.”

People are tired of all the anger. If we can change the direction of political conversations in America, that will be something our grandchildren will be proud to brag about. We're doing this for America.

We are a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. We are mostly run by students – America’s future leaders.

We have student writers, coders, video producers, social media types, fundraisers and more. We are completely virtual and nobody’s getting paid.

Gen Z is inheriting a challenging world and we want to provide this up-and-coming generation with the tools Gen Z will need to cope – and thrive, even.

While our interns are great, they can only do so much. They have school, other jobs and other commitments that cause them to only be able to provide maybe 5 hours a week.

At the end of every semester, around 20 of our 65 interns leave. It takes a while to get the replacement interns up to speed.

I am 74 and could use some help. It is pretty much me and my small army of interns. My students need more adult supervision.

Today’s students are frightened. Too many have given up hope. They need an ongoing pep talk, followed by experiences that indicate they really can make a difference.

In order to take ONC to the next level, it’s time to get more “adults” into the mix. We also need to raise money and pay people, including our interns. It’s time to institutionalize what we’re doing and engage in marketing that will put ONC on the map.

We are willing to pay a 10% success fee to those who raise money for us. Once we raise money, we want to add our Executive Director (and others) to the payroll.

This is a volunteer role, to start. I think the role requires a minimum of 10-20 hours a week.

Get in touch and I'll send you a pitch deck. We have a lot of exciting projects in the works; I need help turning them all into reality. I look forward to hearing from you.

Whether you are navigating compliance, collaborating with the Board of Directors, or visiting our manufacturing sites to raise awareness, your leadership will directly support employees when they need it most.

Strategic Leadership & Global Expansion
Drive Vision: Provide overall leadership and direction for the PEAF, aligning the program with ProAmpac's core values: Integrity, Intensity, Innovation, Involvement, and Impact.
Expand Our Reach: Lead the expansion of the fund to international locations and newly acquired manufacturing sites, adapting processes to respect regional HR policies and practices.
Growth Strategy: Develop and execute strategic plans to scale program participation, overall funding, and community impact.
Program Administration & Compliance
Daily Operations: Oversee the day-to-day administration of the grant process, ensuring applications are handled fairly, efficiently, and with the strictest confidentiality.
Regulatory Compliance: Maintain rigorous records of all grants, donor contributions, and fund activities. Ensure full compliance with nonprofit governance, tax regulations, and legal guidelines.
Digital Resources: Manage the PEAF website and promotional materials to ensure easy, seamless access to applications and contribution portals.

Reporting: Prepare and deliver program metrics, financial updates, and impact reports for board meetings.
Fundraising: Design and champion creative fundraising initiatives, including annual donor campaigns, employee payroll deduction programs, and special events.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Nonprofit Management, Business Administration, Human Resources, or a closely related field preferred.
Experience: Proven experience managing charitable programs, foundation grants, or corporate employee assistance funds (required).
Global Exposure: Demonstrated ability to implement initiatives or lead programs across global, multi-site, or newly acquired organizational footprints.
Financial Acumen: Strong program administration skills with experience in budgeting, financial reporting, and donor tracking.

Key Competencies

Strategic Leadership: Ability to think long-term and transition ideas into highly structured, compliant global programs.
Empathetic Communication: Exceptional relationship-building skills to connect with plant floor employees, executive leadership, and board members alike.
Nonprofit Governance: Deep understanding of regulatory compliance, IRS guidelines for charitable funds, and board administration.

Growth in active employee participation and total recurring contributions.
Awareness increases across all manufacturing and corporate sites.
Efficiency in processing and distributing critical grants equitably.
Seamless onboarding of global sites and newly acquired locations into the program.

Travel & Physical Requirements

Travel: Ability to travel 20-25% to various corporate and manufacturing locations to promote fund awareness and build community relationships.

Overview

At PNNL, our core capabilities are divided among major departments that we refer to as Directorates within the Lab, focused on a specific area of scientific research or other function, with its own leadership team and dedicated budget.

Our Science & Technology directorates include National Security, Integrated Discovery Sciences, and Energy and Environment. In addition, we have an Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, a Department of Energy, Office of Science user facility housed on the PNNL campus.

The Integrated Discovery Sciences Directorate (IDSD) leads fundamental research across biology, chemistry, Earth and environmental sciences, materials science, advanced computing, artificial intelligence, quantum information science, mathematics, autonomy, and DOE national user facilities. Our vision is to accelerate scientific discovery by observing, understanding, simulating, predicting, and controlling dynamic biotic-abiotic processes and interactions within complex biological, chemical, material, and Earth systems. We intentionally connect disciplines to advance fundamental discovery science, develop transformative scientific capabilities, and address the nation's most important challenges in energy, environmental resilience, biotechnology, advanced manufacturing, health, and national security.

Responsibilities

The Office of the Chief Operating Officer (COO) for the Integrated Discovery Sciences Directorate (IDSD) is seeking an experienced administrative professional to serve as a trusted partner to the COO. The successful candidate will bring sound judgment, exceptional discretion, professional composure, and a high degree of independence. The role also requires practical fluency with approved AI-enabled productivity tools and the ability to use them responsibly to improve the quality, speed, and consistency of administrative work.

Because close coordination, accessibility, and real-time partnership are central to the role, this position is expected to work primarily onsite, aligned with the COO's schedule and directorate business needs. The preference for this role is to be onsite at least 4 days a week.

Principal Duties

Use approved AI-enabled tools and automation capabilities to support drafting, summarization, information organization, meeting preparation, and workflow improvement while validating accuracy and protecting sensitive information in accordance with PNNL requirements.
Develop and maintain effective systems for organizing information, tracking commitments, monitoring deadlines, and ensuring timely completion of high-priority activities.

Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is a world-class research institution powered by a highly educated, diverse workforce committed to the values of Integrity, Creativity, Collaboration, Impact, and Courage. Every year, scores of dynamic, driven people come to PNNL to work with renowned researchers on meaningful science, innovations and outcomes for the U.S. Department of Energy and other sponsors; here is your chance to be one of them!

At PNNL, you will find an exciting research environment and excellent benefits including health insurance, and flexible work schedules. PNNL is located in eastern Washington State—the dry side of Washington known for its stellar outdoor recreation and affordable cost of living. Commitment to Excellence and Equal Employment Opportunity

Our laboratory is committed to fostering a work environment where all individuals are treated with fairness and respect while solving critical challenges in fundamental sciences, national security, and energy resiliency. We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

PNNL considers all applicants for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information (including family medical history), protected veteran status, and any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local laws.

To obtain this credential, new employees must successfully complete the applicable tier of federal background investigation post hire and receive a favorable federal adjudication. The tier of federal background investigation will be determined by job duties and national security or public trust responsibilities associated with the job. All tiers of investigation include a declaration of illegal drug activities, including use, supply, possession, or manufacture within the last 1 to 7 years (depending on the applicable tier of investigation). Illegal drug activities include marijuana and cannabis derivatives, which are still considered illegal under federal law, regardless of state laws.

If you are offered a position at PNNL and currently have any affiliation with the government of one of these countries, you will be required to disclose this information and recuse yourself of that affiliation or receive approval from DOE and Battelle prior to your first day of employment.

Our students write articles, host podcasts and sponsor events. We even wrote a book!

We also keep things civil at all times. Republicans, Democrats, Independents -- all are welcome at OUR NATIONAL CONVERSATION (ONC).

In our conversations, we always strive to answer the question, "What do we want to DO about this?" We find, by focusing on solutions, we can quickly rise above the "blame game" which has become so stale in our country.

We seek to make ONC a household name one day -- a trusted source of fair, accurate and balanced information about politics and public policy. Young people are inheriting a troubled world.

At ONC, we are developing America's future leaders, equipping them with skills they will need as they take it from here. Over 900 interns from across the U.S. have participated so far. Experienced mentors gently guide our students.

You can find us at https //www.ournationalconversation.org/.

,

Greetings from OUR NATIONAL CONVERSATION.

My name is Jeff Hall, Editor & CEO at OUR NATIONAL CONVERSATION, or ONC for short.

I’m a newspaper guy going way back. I’m a former VP at the Los Angeles Times and I worked at the White House for a year as something called a White House Fellow. I’m a Stanford grad and a Harvard MBA.

I’ve always operated at the intersection of journalism, public policy and entrepreneurship.

At OUR NATIONAL CONVERSATION, we host nonpartisan, civil conversations about politics. Our goal is to reduce toxic partisanship in America and get America talking again. Our slogan “Less hate, more debate.”

People are tired of all the anger. If we can change the direction of political conversations in America, that will be something our grandchildren will be proud to brag about. We're doing this for America.

We are a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. We are mostly run by students – America’s future leaders.

We have student writers, coders, video producers, social media types, fundraisers and more. We are completely virtual and nobody’s getting paid.

Gen Z is inheriting a challenging world and we want to provide this up-and-coming generation with the tools Gen Z will need to cope – and thrive, even.

While our interns are great, they can only do so much. They have school, other jobs and other commitments that cause them to only be able to provide maybe 5 hours a week.

At the end of every semester, around 20 of our 65 interns leave. It takes a while to get the replacement interns up to speed.

I am 74 and could use some help. It is pretty much me and my small army of interns. My students need more adult supervision.

Today’s students are frightened. Too many have given up hope. They need an ongoing pep talk, followed by experiences that indicate they really can make a difference.

In order to take ONC to the next level, it’s time to get more “adults” into the mix. We also need to raise money and pay people, including our interns. It’s time to institutionalize what we’re doing and engage in marketing that will put ONC on the map.

We are willing to pay a 10% success fee to those who raise money for us. Once we raise money, we want to add our Executive Director (and others) to the payroll.

This is a volunteer role, to start. I think the role requires a minimum of 10-20 hours a week.

Get in touch and I'll send you a pitch deck. We have a lot of exciting projects in the works; I need help turning them all into reality. I look forward to hearing from you.
